userStories.title: Classify and stamp advisory retirement
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give recurrence classification a terminal advisory-retirement bucket and immutable disposition stamps.

**Motivation** — carried sub-threshold findings have no exit.

**Approach** — The recurrence count is computed for every finding; the severity gate then selects which cap applies.

**Scope** — In: recurrence types, algorithm, enabled-mode stamps, inline config shapes. Out: schemas (US-002), mapper/operation wiring (US-003), prompt/fix lane (US-004).

**Interface** — Target `RecurrenceConfig` is `{ enabled: boolean; maxBlockingRounds: number; maxAdvisoryRounds?: number }`; target `RecurrenceResult` is `{ blocking: T[]; advisory: T[]; demoted: T[]; retired: T[]; classified: T[] }`; `RecurrenceCandidate` gains `meta?: Record<string, unknown>`. The optional cap defaults to `2` inside `classifyRecurrence`; enabled-mode stamps are `{ disposition, rounds, wasBlocking }`.
acceptanceCriteria: classifyRecurrence returns retired and classified arrays in addition to blocking, advisory and demoted.
Given warning severity at error threshold and fewer appearances than maxAdvisoryRounds, classifyRecurrence returns the finding in advisory and not retired.
Given a sub-threshold finding whose current-inclusive count is at or above maxAdvisoryRounds, classifyRecurrence returns it in retired and not advisory.
Given an error finding whose current-inclusive count is at or above maxBlockingRounds + 1, classifyRecurrence returns it in demoted and not retired.
Given cfg omits maxAdvisoryRounds and a current-inclusive sub-threshold count of 2, classifyRecurrence retires the finding, applying the documented default.
Each classified finding has meta.recurrence.disposition equal to its bucket name: blocking, advisory, demoted, or retired.
A demoted finding has meta.recurrence.wasBlocking true.
A retired finding has meta.recurrence.wasBlocking false.
Each classified finding has meta.recurrence.rounds equal to its prior appearance count plus one.
classified has one entry per input finding in input order.
Given an input whose meta is absent, after classifyRecurrence its input meta remains absent.
Given unrelated input meta, classified retains it alongside meta.recurrence.
When cfg.enabled is false, classifyRecurrence returns retired as an empty array.
When cfg.enabled is false, classified findings carry no meta.recurrence.
When cfg.enabled is false, classifyRecurrence partitions blocking and advisory by severity alone, matching its behaviour before this feature.
Given no acIndex, classifyRecurrence uses the existing file/category/issue-prefix fallback and disposition is unaffected by missing acIndex.
When priorIterations is empty, classifyRecurrence returns retired as an empty array.
When priorIterations is empty, all classified entries have recurrence.rounds 1.
Given blocking-or-higher test-gap severity in a test file, classifyRecurrence returns it in blocking regardless of count.
Given below-threshold test-gap severity in a test file, classifyRecurrence does not return it in blocking.
Given meta.recurrence, tagCoverageGap returns a finding retaining recurrence and with coverageGap true.

routing.reasoning: Changes a shared classification algorithm and type contracts while reusing established helpers.

outOfScope: the wording of the reviewer prompt; the `meta.coverageGap` tag's own semantics, which are unchanged.

userStories.title: Configure advisory recurrence cap
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make advisory retirement cap a validated resolved config value.

**Motivation** — carried sub-threshold findings have no exit.

**Approach** — `maxAdvisoryRounds: z.number().int().min(1).default(2)` is added to both recurrenceDemotion schemas, with semantic enabled default left at false.

**Scope** — In: schemas and exact-default assertions. Out: classifier runtime default (US-001) and operation wiring (US-003).
acceptanceCriteria: When adversarial recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is unset, resolved config value is 2.
When semantic recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is unset, resolved config value is 2.
When semantic recurrenceDemotion.enabled is unset, resolved config value is false.
When either recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is 0, schema validation rejects the config.
When adversarial recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is 5, resolved config value is 5, so the cap is configuration rather than a literal.

routing.reasoning: A paired additive Zod default and validation rule has direct existing tests.

outOfScope: the runtime default `classifyRecurrence` applies when the field is absent from a caller-supplied config object, which US-001 owns.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test at `:6-9` asserts `expect(parsed.recurrenceDemotion).toEqual({ enabled: true, maxBlockingRounds: 2 })`, and `:10-15` makes the same exact-object assertion for the override case. `toEqual` is exact, so the schema's new `maxAdvisoryRounds` default fails both against a correct implementation. US-002 owns updating them to the new invariant: the parsed object also carries `maxAdvisoryRounds: 2`.

the assertion at `:113` pins `result.data.review.semantic` with `toEqual`, including a nested `recurrenceDemotion: { enabled: false, maxBlockingRounds: 2 }`. The new schema default breaks it against a correct implementation. US-002 owns updating it to the new invariant: the nested object also carries `maxAdvisoryRounds: 2`.

userStories.title: Persist recurrence dispositions through review outputs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve stamps through LLM mappers and expose classified raw findings in review/audit output.

**Motivation** — a passing record can carry an `error` finding with no explanation.

**Approach** — Both LLM finding types gain optional `meta`; both mappers add one allowlist line forwarding `recurrence`. The review audit persists the **raw op shape**, so a LLM stamp reaches `ReviewAuditEntry.result.findings` directly through `review-decision.ts:92`. Operations persist `classified` as findings and fold retired into advisoryFindings.

**Scope** — In: LLM types, mapper allowlists, verify output buckets/logging, audit passthrough. Out: passed computation, semantic default enablement, prompt/fix behavior (US-004).
acceptanceCriteria: Given adversarial LLM meta.recurrence, toAdversarialReviewFindings returns Finding meta.recurrence with the same disposition, rounds and wasBlocking.
Given no adversarial LLM meta, toAdversarialReviewFindings returns Finding meta with no recurrence key.
Given adversarial LLM recurrence and verifiedBy, toAdversarialReviewFindings retains both recurrence and verifiedBy.
Given semantic LLM meta.recurrence, llmFindingToFinding returns Finding meta.recurrence with the same values.
adversarialReviewOp.verify returns one stamped findings entry per accepted finding.
adversarialReviewOp.verify advisoryFindings includes every retired entry in addition to advisory, demoted and AC-dropped entries it already carries.
adversarialReviewOp.verify normalizedFindings contains only blocking entries, so retired is never routable to rectification.
Given warning severity and same-fingerprint priors reaching maxAdvisoryRounds, adversarialReviewOp.verify returns the finding in advisoryFindings stamped retired.
When retired is non-empty, adversarialReviewOp.verify emits one info review-channel log per finding with event review.adversarial.recurrence_retired, file and category.
When a finding is demoted, adversarialReviewOp.verify still emits once per demoted finding the existing review.adversarial.recurrence_demoted log.
Given semantic recurrenceDemotion.enabled true, semanticReviewOp.verify returns one stamped findings entry per accepted finding.
With semantic recurrenceDemotion.enabled at its false default, semanticReviewOp.verify advisoryFindings entries carry no meta.recurrence.

Given adversarial verify findings with recurrence, a built review-audit entry exposes them under result.findings so passed true can distinguish demoted error from miscomputed verdict without replaying demotion state.
Given a demoted error and empty blocking, adversarialReviewOp.verify returns passed true, so the verdict rule at adversarial-review.ts:512 is unchanged by this feature.

routing.reasoning: Five existing modules require straightforward data-flow and log wiring without a new abstraction.

outOfScope: the computation of `passed`; enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review, whose default stays `false`.

modifiedFiles.reason: assertions over the rendered block's finding count and its verdict template. Under AC 1 and AC 5 a retired entry leaves the verdict list and the template count drops accordingly, so any count-based expectation over a fixture containing a stamped entry fails against a correct implementation. US-003 owns updating them to the new invariant: the verdict list and its template count only entries not stamped `disposition: "retired"`, and retired entries appear once in the acknowledgement section.

userStories.title: Acknowledge retired findings and exclude them from fix seeding
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep retired findings visible while removing mandated re-flagging and fix eligibility.

**Motivation** — The only way to stop a reviewer re-raising a true finding is to keep telling it about the finding.

**Approach** — retirement is a **rendering** change: the finding stays in the store and stays in the prompt, but moves out of the verdict list — which requires a per-item classification and mandates identical re-flagging — into an acknowledgement block that states it is closed and must not be re-flagged. The verdict template counts only non-retired entries. `actionableAdvisoryFindings` additionally drops `meta.recurrence.disposition === "retired"` at its seeding site.

**Scope** — In: rendering partition/template counts and advisory seed filtering. Out: store/report removal, still-blocking wording, semantic advisory seeding.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an iteration with a retired finding, buildPriorIterationsBlock verdict-required list omits it.
Given that iteration, buildPriorIterationsBlock acknowledgement section names its file and category.
The acknowledgement section states listed findings are closed and must not be re-flagged, so the still-blocking instruction at prior-iterations-builder.ts:115 does not apply to them.
Given findings with no recurrence meta, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns the block it returns today, so rounds recorded before this feature render unchanged.
buildPriorIterationsBlock verdict template count includes only non-retired findings.
Given an iteration all retired, buildPriorIterationsBlock contains no verdict-required list.
Given three rounds where warning appears in round 1 and reaches maxAdvisoryRounds in round 2, the round-3 prior block lists it only in acknowledgement.
Given retired recurrence disposition, actionableAdvisoryFindings omits the finding.
Given advisory recurrence disposition, actionableAdvisoryFindings includes the finding.
actionableAdvisoryFindings continues to omit actionRequired false and acDropped true findings.
Given a green execution-plan round whose only adversarial advisory findings are retired, the filtered advisory count is zero and no non-blocking fix pass is dispatched.

routing.reasoning: Established prompt rendering and seed filtering change with legacy compatibility and one orchestrator integration check.

outOfScope: the run-end advisory report surface, which continues to read `advisoryFindings` and therefore still lists retired findings.

analysis: Cross-cutting TypeScript enhancement. Current classifyRecurrence has only three buckets and returns at its severity gate before counting sub-threshold recurrence (src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:137-216); its existing fingerprint/count helpers supply AC and prose fallback identity (src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:84-131). Implement immutable classified output, preserved meta, blocking-only test-gap behavior, and disabled-mode legacy behavior. Operations use old config/result fields (src/operations/adversarial-review.ts:479-539; src/operations/semantic-review.ts:425-469). Mapper meta is a closed allowlist (src/review/adversarial-helpers.ts:141-171; src/review/semantic-helpers.ts:188-209), requiring type and mapper changes. Schema defaults and inline shapes require the new cap (src/config/schemas-review.ts:77-82,135-140; src/review/types.ts:132,258). Prompt rendering maps all stored history and counts all entries today (src/prompts/builders/prior-iterations-builder.ts:47-127), so retirement must partition rendering while leaving untagged history unchanged. The seed filter is at src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60 and execution-plan passes the filtered count to shouldRunNonBlockingFix (src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts:402-412). Risks: mutation, dropped meta, changed passed semantics, blocking retirement, and size limits. Migration: optional runtime cap defaults to 2; disabled mode and unstamped historical findings preserve old behavior.
outOfScope: The nax#1910 step-3 analyzer over `review-audit/*.json` — measured 2026-09-10 at 11.1% `unmatched` on 27 sub-threshold findings from a single feature, too small a sample to justify building it.

Retiring a finding on `meta.evidence.status === "unmatched"`. All three `unmatched` findings in the measured corpus were substantive defects, so evidence status measures quote hygiene rather than finding validity and must not gate retirement.
Seeding the non-blocking-fix lane from semantic-review's advisory bucket, tracked as nax#1957 and gated on the nax#1801 ruling.
Changing how `passed` is computed at `adversarial-review.ts:512`. A record carrying `passed: true` beside a demoted `error` keeps that verdict and explains it.
Enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review. The schema field is wired, the default stays `false`, and flipping it is a separate decision needing its own baseline.
The "whack-a-mole within a file" failure where each round yields genuinely new findings, tracked as nax#1157.
Excluding `acDropped` findings from the non-blocking-fix seed. That filter at `non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60` is an existing hold on nax#1801 and is left exactly as it stands.
Changing the `still-blocking` instruction at `prior-iterations-builder.ts:115`. Retirement works by moving a finding out of the verdict list, not by softening the instruction that governs the list.
Similarity-clustering or otherwise changing `fingerprintFor`. Retirement inherits whatever recurrence identity that function already provides.
Dropping retired findings from the iteration store or from `advisoryFindings`. They remain stored and remain reported; only their prompt rendering and their fix-lane eligibility change.
